NATURAL-LANGUAGE HYPOTHESIS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

In the **100-year bin labeled BCE 1700 — the 18th century BCE, spanning approximately BCE 1800 → 1701** — the z-scored diversity of **Pottery Form** shows a sharp decline (Δz_form = −1.87 z-units; form falls from +0.74 at BCE 1800 to its dataset minimum of −1.13 at BCE 1700) **while at the same time** the z-scored diversity of **Pottery Decoration** shows a significant increase (Δz_decor = +1.45 z-units; decoration rises from −0.48 at BCE 1800 to +0.97 at BCE 1700). This is the **first** century in the BCE 4300 → 500 record in which the two series display statistically large opposite-direction first differences — and, in fact, the **only** century where form and decoration move in opposite directions at all.

HYPOTHESIS (DiscoveryBench one-liner)
───────────────────────────────────────
The century is the **18th century BCE — the bin labelled BCE 1700, ≈ BCE 1800 → 1701**. There, Pottery Decoration diversity rises by Δz = +1.45 sd (from −0.48 to +0.97) while Pottery Form diversity falls by Δz = −1.87 sd (from +0.74 to −1.13). This is the first (and only) such oppositional century in the 100-year BCE 4300 → 500 record.

DATA-GROUNDED RATIONALE
────────────────────────────────────
Primary statistic — first difference of z-values between adjacent 100-year bins:
   Δz_form(BCE 1700)  =  ZKeform(1700) − ZKeform(1800) = −1.13 − 0.74 = −1.87
   Δz_decor(BCE 1700) = Zkeverz(1700) − Zkeverz(1800) = +0.97 − (−0.48) = +1.45
   ⇒ form down by 1.87 sd, decoration up by 1.45 sd; magnitudes far exceed any 0.10–1.00 sd threshold.

Threshold sweep on absolute Δz (in z-units) — earliest qualifying bin per threshold:
   T=0.10 sd → BCE 1700      T=0.20 sd → BCE 1700
   T=0.30 sd → BCE 1700   ← default        T=0.50 sd → BCE 1700
   T=1.00 sd → BCE 1700
   ⇒ BCE 1700 is the **only** oppositional bin across the entire 100-year record, at every threshold tested.

Relative-growth sensitivity Δz/|z_prev| (thresholds 0.30, 0.50, 1.00, 2.00) → BCE 1700 in all loose variants.

Cross-validation against `PotteryForm_inter` / `PotteryDecoration_inter` from `time_series_data.csv`: at 36 century anchors BCE 4000 → 500, cap_Δz == ts_Δz exactly (max abs diff < 1e-6); **0 disagreements / 36 checks** ⇒ answer is robust to source-file choice.

Continuity caveat (transparent, per protocol): the strict continuity rule (same sign on the immediately previous older bin) is **not** satisfied at BCE 1700 because BCE 1800 had Δz_form = +0.15 (form UP, not down) and Δz_decor = +0.11 (also UP). The form collapse at BCE 1700 is therefore a **punctuated discontinuous cliff**, not the second leg of a sustained two-century decline. Given the magnitude (|Δ| ≈ 1.6–2.5 sd) and uniqueness across 37 bins, this is best read as a genuine punctuated transition, not noise.

Post-event readout (BCE 1700 → 500): no later bin simultaneously satisfies both conditions because ZKeform is locked at −1.13 (its dataset minimum) for the next 12 centuries with Δz = 0; the only non-trivial post-1700 step is +0.56 sd at BCE 1000 in Zkeverz (+0.97 → +1.53), but form is flat there ⇒ not oppositional. So BCE 1700 is **both the earliest and the latest** qualifying bin in the record.

Padding-row note (per protocol item a): capital.csv rows at BCE 4300 and BCE 4200 replicate the BCE 4100 anchor z-values, giving Δz = 0 by construction. They were excluded; the first evaluable century is BCE 4100.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

payload.hypothesis: The first century in which diversity in Pottery Form and diversity in Pottery Decoration show opposite growth trends, with Pottery Decoration significantly increasing and Pottery Form simultaneously declining, is the 18th century BCE (the 100-year bin labelled BCE 1700, ≈ BCE 1800 → 1701). There, Δz_form = −1.87 (z-form falls from +0.74 to its dataset minimum −1.13) co-occurs with Δz_decor = +1.45 (z-decoration rises from −0.48 to +0.97). This is the only century throughout the 100-year BCE 4300 → 500 record in which the two series move in opposite directions: the finding is stable across absolute Δz thresholds {0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50, 1.00} sd, across a relative-growth sensitivity sweep at Δz/|z_prev| thresholds {0.30, 0.50, 1.00, 2.00}, and against cross-validation with time_series_data.csv's PotteryForm_inter / PotteryDecoration_inter at all 36 century anchors (zero disagreements). The strict continuity-on-prior-bin filter is not satisfied because BCE 1800 has form-UP (+0.15); the form decline at BCE 1700 is therefore best characterized as a punctuated transition rather than the second leg of a sustained two-century trend. No later bin can be oppositional because Pottery Form remains pinned at −1.13 from BCE 1700 → 500.
payload.workflow: (1) Loaded capital.csv (15 cols × 39 rows, BCE 500..4300 at 100-year bins), converted European comma decimals; loaded time_series_data.csv (37 cols × 3601 rows, CE −4100..−500 at 1-year resolution). (2) Excluded padding rows BCE 4300 and BCE 4200 (they duplicate the BCE-4100 anchor by construction); the first evaluable century is BCE 4100. (3) Computed first differences Δz(BCE_t) = z(BCE_t) − z(BCE_{t+100}) for ZKeform and Zkeverz on capital.csv. (4) Operationalized "significant increase of Decoration / decline of Form" as Δz_decor > +T and Δz_form < −T for T ∈ {0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50, 1.00} sd; reported both the loose setting and a continuity-strengthened (same-sign on previous older bin) variant. (5) Added a relative-growth sensitivity Δz/|z_prev| ∈ {0.30, 0.50, 1.00, 2.00}. (6) Cross-validated every bin's Δz against time_series_data.csv's PotteryForm_inter / PotteryDecoration_inter at century boundaries (BCE 4100 is skipped because its older anchor at CE = −4200 is outside time_series). (7) Saved diagnostics.csv, sweep.json, and the analysis script. Headline result: BCE 1700 is the unique oppositional century under every threshold tested.
